blocks.text: Nightly inventory extract: on-call SOP

This is the runbook for extract_inv.sh and load_inv.py. If you are holding #oakridge-inv-oncall at 02:15 ET because the file is missing, start at When the file is missing at 02:15. Do not start by SSHing to the IBM i. Do not start by rerunning Crystal. The path is batch-01.oak.internal (extract), files.oak.internal (drop), forgenet-ro-01.oak.internal (load). Window is 01:10-02:15 Eastern. Author: Aman Kumar. Walt Hendricks owns the scripts. I own this document because Walt writes scripts and does not write SOPs, and Priya Nair got tired of him being the only person who could run this cold.
VP skim: Purpose and window, then Freeze at Fort Wayne, then Who to page. Engineer at 2am: Preconditions, the exact commands, truncated-file detection, missing-file page, freeze handling, rollback.
Purpose and window

Every night we pull inventory position off ForgeNet 7.4 (via the INV_READ account Walt set up against the IBM i companion extract, then sqlplus against the staging Oracle on batch-01 that already has the pulled tables) and land a CSV plus trailer on sftp://files.oak.internal/inv/in. load_inv.py on inv-api-01 (Walt also installed it on batch-01 as a fallback) sqlldr's into the replica views' base tables. inventory-api reads the replica. If this job dies, Tom Rourke's tablet goes stale and Crystal is the only number, which is the 2018 problem we just crawled out of.

Window: 01:10 ET start, 02:15 ET hard 'file must exist' check. Typical runtime 38-44 minutes for all four plants. Dayton is 62% of the bytes. A Fort Wayne freeze night is faster (plant 02 section is a stub) and you must still produce a file. Sunday nights usually run. Greenville OPEN_INV=N on Sunday does not skip the extract; the API surfaces PLANT_CLOSED. We still extract.

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: If INV_YYYYMMDD_*.csv is absent from files.oak.internal:/inv/in at 02:15 ET, page #oakridge-inv-oncall and then follow When the file is missing. Do not wait until 06:00 for Tom to notice. The 02:15 cron on batch-01 already pages. If you are on call you acknowledge within 10 minutes even if you then call Walt.
Preconditions (check these before you touch anything)

items: You are on FortiClient profile Oakridge-Plant-SSL (not Oakridge-Corp, not the 2018 profile). ping batch-01.oak.internal (10.24.8.33), files.oak.internal (10.24.8.19), forgenet-ro-01.oak.internal (10.24.9.7), inv-api-01.oak.internal (10.24.8.41).
Your uid can sudo -u invextract on batch-01, or you have the break-glass key in 1Password vault Oakridge-INV, item batch-01-invextract. If you do not, page Walt and Elena Vasquez. Do not ssh as root.
You know whether tonight is a Fort Wayne freeze night. Check the plant calendar before you decide the 02 section 'looks too small' and rerun. Command below.
You are not in the middle of Walt's apply. If replica lag is already over 180s at 00:50, the previous load may still be running. Do not stack a second sqlldr.
Crystal on rpt-01 is not your recovery path for the API. It reads the same drop. If the drop is missing, Crystal is missing too.

blocks.text: What 'healthy' looks like

# 1) On batch-01, as you, then sudo.
ssh -l $USER batch-01.oak.internal
sudo -u invextract -i
cd /opt/oak/inv
ls -l extract_inv.sh load_inv.py   # both should exist; load_inv.py is a copy, canonical is on inv-api-01

# 2) Last night's log. Dates are ET because the box is America/New_York.
tail -n 80 /var/log/oak/inv/extract_$(date +%Y%m%d).log
# Look for: 'trailer COUNT=' and 'sftp put ok' and no 'TRUNCATED'.

# 3) Drop. From batch-01 or your laptop on VPN.
sftp invsftp@files.oak.internal
cd inv/in
ls -l INV_$(date +%Y%m%d)*
# Expect two files: INV_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.csv and INV_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.trl
# Typical csv size: 1.12G-1.34G. Under 400M on a non-freeze night is a truncated or plant-missing file.

# 4) Trailer contents (single line).
get INV_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.trl
# COUNT=18442011 FROZEN=N PLANTS=01,02,03,04 SHA256=<hex>
# COUNT is data rows, not including header. FROZEN=Y means Fort Wayne freeze stub.

# 5) Replica lag from inv-api-01 after load (load cron 02:05-ish).
ssh inv-api-01.oak.internal
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8084/health
# {"status":"UP","replicaLagMs":2410,"redis":"UP","lastLoad":"2020-03-12T07:08:12Z"}
# replicaLagMs over 180000 after 02:40 is a load problem. Page.
blocks.caption: Healthy-night checks. Run 3-5 in this order if you were just paged; skip 1-2 until you know the file is actually missing.

blocks.text: The job, when you have to run it by hand
Preconditions specific to a manual run

Only rerun if the 01:10 cron did not start, or it started and died before sftp, or the trailer is missing. If a file exists with a valid trailer and sqlldr is running, do not start a second extract. You will race the loader. If you are not sure, check load_inv.py with ps on inv-api-01.

items: On inv-api-01: ps -ef | grep -E 'load_inv|sqlldr' | grep -v grep. If it is running, wait or talk to Walt. Do not extract in parallel.
On batch-01 as invextract: confirm no extract_inv.sh already running. pgrep -af extract_inv.sh
Check freeze (see Fort Wayne section). Export OAK_FW_FREEZE=Y or N explicitly. Do not rely on auto-detect if PLANT_CAL is the thing you do not trust tonight.
Run the extract. Stay attached. Do not nohup the first time you ever run this; you want the sqlplus errors in your face.

Verify trailer COUNT vs wc -l of the csv minus 1 (header). If they disagree, do not sftp. The script should refuse. If you overrode, you made Crystal and the API load a short file. That is October 27.
If you had to sftp by hand, run load_inv.py on inv-api-01 against the new file. Do not load a file with a mismatched trailer.

blocks.text:
# Manual extract on batch-01. Window after a failed 01:10 run, still before 05:00 if you can.
# After 05:00 Tom's huddle is in play; say so in #oakridge-inv-oncall.

sudo -u invextract -i
cd /opt/oak/inv
umask 027

# Freeze flag. Read it, do not guess.
sqlplus -s INV_READ/$(cat /etc/oak/inv/inv_read.pw)@//localhost:1521/INVSTG <<'SQL'
SET HEADING OFF FEEDBACK OFF PAGES 0
SELECT PLANT||' '||FREEZE_INV||' '||OPEN_INV
  FROM PLANT_CAL
 WHERE CAL_DT = TRUNC(SYSDATE)
   AND PLANT IN ('01','02','03','04')
 ORDER BY PLANT;
EXIT
SQL
# Expect four lines like: 02 Y N   on a Fort Wayne freeze night.
# Plant is CHAR(2). If you see 2 Y N you are in the integer footgun. Stop. Call Walt.

export OAK_FW_FREEZE=$(sqlplus -s INV_READ/$(cat /etc/oak/inv/inv_read.pw)@//localhost:1521/INVSTG <<'SQL'
SET HEADING OFF FEEDBACK OFF PAGES 0
SELECT TRIM(FREEZE_INV) FROM PLANT_CAL
 WHERE CAL_DT = TRUNC(SYSDATE) AND PLANT = '02';
EXIT
SQL
)
# TRIM only on FREEZE_INV (Y/N), never on PLANT.

# Run. Script lives here. It spools /var/tmp/oak/inv/INV_<ts>.csv then sftps.
./extract_inv.sh
# Logs: /var/log/oak/inv/extract_YYYYMMDD.log
# Exit 0 = trailer written and sftp put ok.
# Exit 2 = sqlplus failed.
# Exit 3 = trailer COUNT mismatch (truncated spool).
# Exit 4 = sftp failed. File may still be in /var/tmp/oak/inv/. Do not delete it.
# Exit 5 = freeze flag in PLANT_CAL is Y but OAK_FW_FREEZE was forced N (script refuses).

echo $?
blocks.caption: Manual extract. extract_inv.sh already calls sqlplus as INV_READ and writes the trailer. You should not spool by hand unless the script is broken and Walt is on the phone.

blocks.text: If you must spool by hand (script is broken)

# Only with Walt on the channel. This is the inner sqlplus the script wraps.
# Spool path MUST be on batch-01 local disk, not an NFS home.

TS=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
OUT=/var/tmp/oak/inv/INV_${TS}.csv
TRL=/var/tmp/oak/inv/INV_${TS}.trl
mkdir -p /var/tmp/oak/inv

sqlplus -s INV_READ/$(cat /etc/oak/inv/inv_read.pw)@//localhost:1521/INVSTG <<SQL
SET COLSEP ','
SET PAGESIZE 0
SET TRIMSPOOL ON
SET LINESIZE 4000
SET FEEDBACK OFF
SET HEADING ON
SPOOL $OUT
SELECT /*+ PARALLEL(4) */ PLANT, ITEM_NO, BIN_CODE, QTY_OH, QTY_HOLD, UOM,
       TO_CHAR(LAST_CNT_TS,'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS') AS LAST_CNT_TS,
       FRZ_FLAG, SERIAL_FLAG
  FROM INV_BIN
 WHERE PLANT IN ('01','02','03','04');
SPOOL OFF
SQL

# Row count minus header. Header is line 1.
ROWS=$(($(wc -l < "$OUT") - 1))
if [ "$ROWS" -lt 1000000 ]; then
  echo "TOO SMALL: $ROWS rows. Refusing trailer. October 27 pattern." >&2
  exit 3
fi

# SHA256 of csv, freeze from env, plants hard-coded.
SHA=$(sha256sum "$OUT" | awk '{print $1}')
printf 'COUNT=%s FROZEN=%s PLANTS=01,02,03,04 SHA256=%s\n' "$ROWS" "${OAK_FW_FREEZE:-N}" "$SHA" > "$TRL"

# SFTP. Batch file so you do not fat-finger cd.
cat > /tmp/sftp.batch <<EOF
cd inv/in
put $OUT
put $TRL
bye
EOF
sftp -b /tmp/sftp.batch -i ~invextract/.ssh/id_sftp_files invsftp@files.oak.internal
rm -f /tmp/sftp.batch
blocks.caption: Hand spool. Parallel(4) is what Walt allows on INVSTG at night. Do not raise it. Do not run this against forgenet-ro-01; that is the replica, not the extract source.

blocks.text: Loader

# On inv-api-01 as invapi (or sudo -u invapi -i)
cd /opt/oak/inv
# load_inv.py finds the newest matching csv+trl pair on the SFTP mount
# (files.oak.internal is mounted at /mnt/files/inv/in on inv-api-01).
# If the mount is stale, ls will lie. Check with a file you just put.

ls -l /mnt/files/inv/in/INV_$(date +%Y%m%d)*

python2.7 load_inv.py --dir /mnt/files/inv/in --date $(date +%Y%m%d)
# python2.7 on purpose. RHEL 7. Do not 'fix' this to python3 at 02:30.
# Exits:
#  0 load ok, replica SCN moved, health lastLoad stamped via a file
#    /var/lib/oak/inv/last_load.json
#  2 no csv
#  3 no trailer
#  4 COUNT mismatch vs wc, or SHA256 mismatch
#  5 sqlldr failed (see /var/log/oak/inv/sqlldr_YYYYMMDD.log)
#  6 freeze trailer FROZEN=Y but plant 02 section has full-size rows
#    (someone extracted Fort Wayne live during physical). Refuse.

# After 0:
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8084/health
# Wait until replicaLagMs is back under 5000 on a quiet night.
# Cycle-count nights 12000-40000 is normal. 180000 is not. Do not bounce Tomcat.
blocks.caption: Loader. sqlldr control file is /opt/oak/inv/inv_bin.ctl. If you edit it at 02:30 without Walt, I will find you.

blocks.text: Truncated file detection

October 27, 2019: Dayton spool filled the 1.0G tmp filesystem, sqlplus kept going in memory, SFTP put a 1.0G file with no trailer, Crystal loaded it, Tom's first-shift numbers were short by roughly the last 40% of Dayton bins. We added the trailer, the COUNT check, the SHA256, and a min-row floor of 1,000,000 on non-freeze nights (freeze nights may be lower because plant 02 is a stub; min-row floor in the script becomes 800,000 when OAK_FW_FREEZE=Y).

rows: No .trl next to a .csv
Script died after spool, or hand-sftp of csv only
Do not load. Do not let Crystal pick it up (see quarantine). Fix disk, rerun extract, put csv+trl together.
COUNT in trl != wc -l minus 1
Partial write, or someone edited the csv
Refuse. Exit 3/4. Rerun extract. Do not 'fix' the trailer to match the short file.
SHA256 mismatch
Transfer corruption or an extra put that overwrote csv but not trl
Refuse. Re-put both from /var/tmp/oak/inv/ on batch-01 if they are still there.
csv size ~1.0G exactly, or 1023M
tmp filesystem cap. df -h /var/tmp
Clear old INV_* in /var/tmp/oak/inv, check df, rerun. If /var/tmp is still tight, spool to /data/oak/inv/spool (1.8T). extract_inv.sh honors OAK_SPOOL_DIR.
Row count 0 or header only
Plant bind as integer, or INV_READ grants dropped
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM INV_BIN WHERE PLANT='01' as INV_READ. If 0, stop and call Walt. Do not sftp an empty file.
load_inv.py exit 6
Freeze trailer vs full Fort Wayne rows
Do not force. See freeze section. Loading live Fort Wayne during physical is how you unfreeze the replica while the floor is frozen.
blocks.caption: Truncation and refuse cases. October 27 is the story you tell yourself before you edit a trailer by hand.

blocks.text: When the file is missing at 02:15

blocks.label: Warn
blocks.text: The pager is cron on batch-01: 15 2 * * * /opt/oak/inv/check_landed.sh. It pages #oakridge-inv-oncall via the plant Slack incoming webhook plus Diego's PagerDuty overlay. Acknowledge in Slack with 'acked <your name>'. Then work the list. Do not ack and go back to sleep.

items: Ack the page in #oakridge-inv-oncall.
VPN Oakridge-Plant-SSL. ping files.oak.internal. If DNS fails you are on the wrong profile. Fix VPN before you declare the drop dead.
sftp ls inv/in for tonight's date. If files exist, check_landed.sh may have raced a late sftp. Run check_landed.sh by hand. If it is happy, say so in channel and stop.
If files do not exist: ssh batch-01, read tonight's extract log. Classify exit code (2 sqlplus, 3 truncate, 4 sftp, 5 freeze mismatch, or cron never fired).
If cron never fired: check crontab -l -u invextract. If the line is missing, someone 'cleaned up' crontabs. Restore from /opt/oak/inv/crontab.invextract and run extract by hand.

If sqlplus failed: do not loop the script 10 times. One retry after a 60s wait. If ORA-01017, INV_READ password rotated and /etc/oak/inv/inv_read.pw was not updated. Elena and Walt. If ORA-01555, snapshot too old on INVSTG, wait 5 minutes, one retry, then Walt.
If sftp failed and local csv+trl exist in /var/tmp/oak/inv: put them. Then run load_inv.py. Then run check_landed.sh.

If you cannot land a valid file by 03:30 ET: post in channel that first shift will be on Crystal, page Priya if it is a weekday, and leave a note for Tom. Do not give Tom a half-loaded replica. A half-load is worse than last night's full load.

If load_inv.py has not run and the file did land: run the loader. Missing file page sometimes fires because the mount on inv-api-01 went stale (NFS). ls /mnt/files/inv/in from inv-api-01; if empty but sftp shows files, sudo mount -o remount /mnt/files and re-ls. Then load.

blocks.text: Do not restart inventory-api.service to 'clear' a missing file. The API will happily serve last night's replica. That is the correct degraded mode until a good load finishes. A Tomcat bounce at 02:22 drops the aisle 7 display and does not extract anything.
Fort Wayne freeze flag

About twice a year Fort Wayne sets PLANT_CAL.FREEZE_INV='Y' for plant '02' for 2-4 days while they do physical. Ken Ibarra (Fort Wayne materials) and Elena send #oakridge-inv-oncall a heads-up the afternoon before. extract_inv.sh in freeze mode writes a stub section for plant 02: header rows plus a single marker line PLANT=02,FROZEN=Y, and omits the 1.87M bin rows. Trailer FROZEN=Y. load_inv.py does not replace Fort Wayne bins on the replica; it leaves yesterday's 02 rows and stamps the freeze on PLANT_CAL. The API then returns X-Oak-Plant-Freeze: Y. This is required. If you 'help' by forcing a full Fort Wayne extract during physical, the replica unfreezes while the floor is frozen and cycle counts collide with picks that are not supposed to happen.

items: Confirm FREEZE_INV for plant '02' and today's CAL_DT. SQL in the manual extract section. Plant bind '02' as a string.
If Y: export OAK_FW_FREEZE=Y before extract_inv.sh. The script also auto-reads PLANT_CAL; the env var is the override when you do not trust auto-read.

If the cron already ran a full 02 section by mistake (trailer FROZEN=N on a freeze night): quarantine that pair, set OAK_FW_FREEZE=Y, rerun extract, load. Then tell Ken Ibarra you may have applied a live 02 snapshot during freeze. He needs that for the physical.
If freeze is N and someone set OAK_FW_FREEZE=Y in a leftover shell: unset it. A stub 02 on a normal night drops Fort Wayne from the tablet.

Do not run extract at 10:00 ET on a freeze day 'to refresh Dayton'. Dayton can wait. A daytime extract contends with INVSTG and with Walt's apply. If Dayton is the emergency, wait for Walt unless replica lag is already dead and Priya says go.

blocks.label: Note
blocks.text: Freeze weeks are not an API outage. If Tom calls because Fort Wayne qty 'looks yesterday', say yes, that is the freeze, and point at exceptions PLANT_FROZEN. Do not rerun extract to make him happier.
Commands to inspect without making it worse

# Replica row counts by plant. INV_API_RO is fine for SELECT.
sqlplus -s INV_API_RO@//forgenet-ro-01.oak.internal:1521/FORGERO <<'SQL'
SET PAGES 20 LINES 80
SELECT PLANT, COUNT(*) CNT FROM INV_BIN GROUP BY PLANT ORDER BY PLANT;
-- Expect ~4.19e6, ~1.87e6, ~2.24e6, ~0.96e6
SELECT PLANT, FREEZE_INV, OPEN_INV FROM PLANT_CAL
 WHERE CAL_DT = TRUNC(SYSDATE AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York')
 ORDER BY PLANT;
EXIT
SQL

# Cron on batch-01
sudo -u invextract crontab -l
# Should contain:
# 10 1 * * * /opt/oak/inv/extract_inv.sh >> /var/log/oak/inv/cron.log 2>&1
# 15 2 * * * /opt/oak/inv/check_landed.sh

# Cron on inv-api-01
sudo -u invapi crontab -l
# 5 2 * * * /usr/bin/python2.7 /opt/oak/inv/load_inv.py --dir /mnt/files/inv/in --date $(date +\%Y\%m\%d)

# Disk on batch-01 spool
df -h /var/tmp /data/oak
ls -lh /var/tmp/oak/inv | tail
blocks.caption: Read-only inspection. The date timezone conversion in PLANT_CAL is easy to get wrong at 02:00 around DST. In March we are past the 2020 US DST change (March 8). Still, if CAL_DT looks like tomorrow, you used UTC.

blocks.text: Rollback and 'we loaded a bad file'

load_inv.py writes a previous-good pointer: /var/lib/oak/inv/last_good.scn and keeps the previous csv on /mnt/files/inv/in/prev/. Rollback is not a full Oracle flashback you run at 02:40 without Walt. Rollback is: stop the loader if it is still running, quarantine the bad pair, ask Walt to apply the prev csv if last_good is intact, or leave last night's replica in place (do nothing) if prev is missing. Doing nothing is valid. Serving last night is better than serving 60% of Dayton. Say that in channel so Tom hears 'stale' instead of 'wrong'.

Rejected recovery: restore from IBM i live query at 02:30 through a developer sqlplus on oak-i5-01. Walt will revoke access. Helix Grid is not a recovery path. Rerunning Crystal against a quarantined csv is how you reprint a truncated PDF. Do not.
